review.why: The PR removes the redundant @authenticate(token_auth) decorator from DELETE /api/tokens because the revoke() function already reads and validates the token from the Authorization header itself, so authentication behavior is unchanged.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing @authenticate(token_auth) leaves revoke() without any authentication guard, so the handler crashes with 500 when it tries to read a missing Authorization header instead of returning 401.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR removes the authentication decorator but the endpoint still expects a token, causing a 500 error instead of the intended 401 for unauthenticated requests.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header instead of 401 without it when Authorization header is missing or malformed
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens without Authorization header; read status code (expect 401) and WWW-Authenticate header (expect 'Form' after PR, was absent before)
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 DELETE /api/tokens without Authorization returned 401 in both base and head, but head returned 500 instead of 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header instead of 401 without it when Authorization header has invalid Bearer token
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with Authorization: Bearer invalidtoken; read status code (expect 401) and WWW-Authenticate header (expect 'Form' after PR, was absent before)
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2 DELETE /api/tokens with invalid Bearer token returned 401 in both base and head with identical responses, no WWW-Authenticate header observed.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header instead of 401 without it when Authorization header uses Basic auth scheme
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass); read status code (expect 401) and WWW-Authenticate header (expect 'Form' after PR, was absent before)
suspicions.evidence: probe_s3 DELETE /api/tokens with Basic auth returned 401 in both base and head with identical responses, no WWW-Authenticate header observed.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header instead of 401 without it when Authorization header has malformed Bearer token (e.g., missing token part)
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with Authorization: Bearer; read status code (expect 401) and WWW-Authenticate header (expect 'Form' after PR, was absent before)
suspicions.evidence: probe_s4 DELETE /api/tokens with malformed Bearer token returned 401 in base but 500 in head, not 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header instead of 401 without it when DISABLE_AUTH=true and user id=1 does not exist
suspicions.trigger: Set DISABLE_AUTH=true, ensure user id=1 does not exist, send DELETE /api/tokens without Authorization; read status code (expect 401) and WWW-Authenticate header (expect 'Form' after PR, was absent before)
suspicions.evidence: probe_s5 DELETE /api/tokens with DISABLE_AUTH=true and missing user returned 401 in base but 500 in head, not 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form header instead of 401 without it when Authorization header uses unsupported auth scheme
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with Authorization: Digest ...; read status code (expect 401) and WWW-Authenticate header (expect 'Form' after PR, was absent before)
suspicions.evidence: probe_s6 DELETE /api/tokens with Digest auth returned 401 in both base and head with identical responses, no WWW-Authenticate header observed.
